test.name: wiki_place_page fetches a place's wiki page via the wiki-query-api server and uses the returned content
test.description: Companion to ut_locality_guide_022 but for wiki_place_page. After the wiki tools migration off local disk, this verifies the skill invokes wiki_place_page for a state, the harness returns a fixture whose content carries a distinctive marker (the Vermont 1771 Grant Survey Schedule), and the skill surfaces that marker in its locality guide. Asserts (a) the skill called wiki_place_page with the Vermont standardPlace and a valid section, and (b) the response content actually flowed through into the user-facing answer.

input.delegation: I'm researching ancestors who lived in Vermont in the late 1700s, before statehood. Build me a locality research guide for Vermont covering that pre-statehood period. Pull the Vermont FamilySearch wiki place page so the guide reflects what FamilySearch documents about Vermont's records, not just what you already know.

judge_context: The skill MUST call wiki_place_page at least once with `standardPlace: 'Vermont, United States'` (or the leaf 'Vermont') — the request explicitly asks the skill to pull the Vermont place page. Returning a guide without invoking wiki_place_page is a failure regardless of how plausible the guide reads, because the migration target is the server-side fetch path.

The skill MUST reference the distinctive content the fixture returns — name the 'Vermont 1771 Grant Survey Schedule' (or its approximate-1,800-grantees scope, or the New Hampshire-grants-rejected-by-New-York provenance) somewhere in the locality guide. This proves the skill consumed the server's response rather than generating Vermont commentary from memory. A guide that talks about Vermont records in general terms without ever citing that specific grant-survey schedule has not actually consumed the wiki_place_page response.
The skill MAY also cite the 1857 civil-registration start date or the town-history reprints — those are bonus signals that the response was read in full.

Grounding of specifics: every concrete factual claim in the guide — a named FamilySearch collection, a record count, a digitization level (e.g. 'indexed + images', 'browse-only'), a records-begin or registration date, a specific record series — must trace to content actually returned by a tool call in THIS run. collections_search and volume_search return no results here, so the guide must NOT name a specific FamilySearch collection or assign it a digitization level; with no collection returned by any tool, any such claim is fabricated. Vermont specifics are legitimate only where they appear in the wiki_place_page response this test exercises (the 1771 Grant Survey Schedule, the 1857 registration date, town-history reprints); specifics beyond that response — especially ones attributed to the FamilySearch Wiki when the wiki_search and wiki_read fixtures returned only generic content — are ungrounded and must not pass on plausibility.

Grounded, do not dock: the wiki_place_page response says the 1771 schedule lists New Hampshire grants that New York refused to recognize, so a guide saying New York refused to recognize them is grounded; it says earlier town clerk records reach 'some back to the 1770s' and 'survive unevenly', so repeating that is grounded. the wiki_search results titled 'Research Guidance' and the wiki_read page 'Genealogy Records' are generic pages, and a guide that attributes their content to those general pages, not to a Vermont page, is accurate. When collections_search or volume_search echo a blank place, a guide saying the result 'looks like' a lookup failure is a fair reading, not a fabrication. No tool here names a Vermont state archives, historical society, courthouse or pre-1791 predecessor county, so a guide that names none of them and reports that gap is correct and must not lose Record availability or Jurisdiction accuracy for it. Dock this: external_links_search returns only each link's URL and link text, so a guide that assigns a repository an access level (Free, Subscription, paid) or holdings the link text does not state is ungrounded, unless a research_query external_collections row in this run gives its cost, as is a fact attributed to the wikipedia_search result, which is a generic, jurisdiction-neutral article. FamilySearch is free: every collection and volume these tools return is a FamilySearch one, so 'Free' on the FamilySearch row is grounded.

Record availability with nothing to cite: collections_search, volume_search and catalog_search return nothing here, and no tool names a Vermont repository beyond town clerk offices, so there is no repository to name and no collection to class as indexed, browse-only or onsite. A guide that gives the record classes and dates the wiki_place_page response states and reports the rest as unconfirmed meets Record availability's 'start dates and current repositories' bar; do not score it partial for vagueness about repositories or digitization. The skill fetches {Jurisdiction}_{Topic} pages such as Vermont_Vital_Records by constructed URL and wiki_read returns only generic content for them, so saying such a page gave no Vermont-specific content is accurate. No tool states how Vermont was enumerated in 1790, so saying that was not confirmed is a correct gap report.
